title: Cylindrical base
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, create the first loop by drawing a single circle with its center at coordinates [0.0147, 0.0147] and a radius of 0.0147. After drawing the circle, apply a scale factor of 0.0293 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Once scaled, transform the sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same translation vector. With the sketch now in 3D space, extrude it along the normal direction by 0.75 units to create the cylindrical base. Ensure that the extrusion does not extend in the opposite direction. This extrusion will form a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical base are a length of 0.02934782608695652 units, a width of 0.02934782608695652 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.code:

wp = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circle with the given center and radius
circle = wp.center(0.0147, 0.0147).circle(0.0147)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
cylinder = circle.extrude(0.75)

# The final model
r = cylinder

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0147, 0.0147)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0147)  # Draw a circle with the specified radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
